questions.q: What is the difference between a reference line and a reference band?
options: A reference band can only be added to maps
A reference line draws a single line at one value; a reference band shades the area between two values
They are the same feature under two different names
A reference line only works on discrete axes; a reference band only works on continuous axes
questions.explain: A reference line marks one constant or computed value with a single line. A reference band shades the area between two constant or computed values.

questions.q: What do the Table, Pane, and Cell scope options control for a reference line or band?
options: Whether the reference line is visible on export vs. on screen
Whether it applies once across the whole view, once per pane (e.g., each row of a small multiple), or once per individual mark grouping
The color of the reference line only
The font size used for the reference line's label
questions.explain: Entire Table applies one reference item across the whole view; Per Pane applies a separate one to each pane of a trellis/small-multiple view; Per Cell applies one to every individual mark grouping.

questions.q: How do you turn a fixed reference line into a dynamic target that a user can move?
options: Convert the reference line into a table calculation
Reference lines can never be made dynamic in Tableau
Set the reference line's Value field to a parameter instead of a constant number
Rename the reference line to include the word 'dynamic'
questions.explain: Pointing a reference line's Value field at a parameter (instead of typing a constant) makes it dynamic — its position now follows whatever value the parameter holds.

questions.q: What makes a dynamic reference line interactive (e.g., moving as a user hovers over marks), rather than just parameter-driven?
options: Setting the reference line's scope to Per Cell
Publishing the workbook to Tableau Server
A parameter action (Dashboard → Actions → Add Action → Change Parameter) that updates the parameter's value based on user interaction like hover
Simply creating the parameter is enough — no further action is needed
questions.explain: A parameter alone just gives the reference line a variable Value field. A parameter action is what actually changes that parameter's value in response to user interaction, like hovering over a mark.

questions.q: In the reference band example shown in this lesson (a small multiple of Consumer, Corporate, and Home Office sales), what scope was used?
options: No scope was applied; the band appears everywhere by default
Entire Table — one single band spanning all three panes combined
Per Cell — a separate band for every single mark
Per Pane — a separate reference band on each of the three panes
questions.explain: The band was applied per pane, giving each of the three small-multiple panes (Consumer, Corporate, Home Office) its own shaded reference range to compare its trend against.
